chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “When one of you has a deceased person, then lay him facing the qiblah. Likewise, when he is washed, a place for washing is dug for him facing the qiblah, so that he is turned with the soles of his feet and his face toward the qiblah.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Then he should prompt him with the testimony that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner; and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger; and that Amīr al-Muʾminīn is the Wali of Allah, the one established in truth after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله; and he should name the Imams one by one so that he may affirm faith in Allah, His Messenger, and his Imams عليهم السلام at the time of his death, and thereby conclude his deeds. If he is able to move his tongue with the testimony in the manner we have mentioned, then he should do so; otherwise, he should bind his heart to it. It is also recommended that he be prompted with the words of relief, which are: There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous; there is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent; glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and whatever is in them and whatever is between them and Lord of the Mighty Throne.
“And peace be upon the messengers. And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
For that is among the things that make easier for him the hardship of what he encounters from the strain of his soul’s departure, to the end of it. This is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام mentioned in the deathbed prompting
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ: the Imams عليهم السلام, named one by one for affirmation at death
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction faced in ritual orientation, toward which the dying and deceased are turned
key_terms.خُرُوجِ نَفْسِهِ: the departure of his soul at death
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ: the testimony of faith recited or prompted at the time of death
key_terms.كَلِمَاتِ الْفَرَجِ: specific words of relief recommended to be prompted to the dying person
key_terms.وَفَاتِهِ: his death, the moment at which these promptings are to be given

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about turning the dying person toward the qiblah and prompting him with the shahadah?
ai.summary: This report discusses the recommended practices for attending a dying person and preparing the deceased, including orienting the person toward the qiblah and prompting him with the shahadah and acknowledgment of the Imams عليهم السلام. It also recommends reciting words of faraj and concludes that these acts help ease the hardship of the soul’s departure at death.
